Virender Singh, Judge Aggrieved from the award, dated 2.12.2015, passed by the Court of learned Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-III, Mandi, District Mandi, H.P. (hereinafter referred to as 'the Tribunal'), in Claim Petition No. 22/2015/2010, titled as, 'Tek Chand versus Thakur Dass & anr.',

2. Vide award impugned herein, the learned Tribunal has allowed the petition, filed by respondent No. 1 Tek Chand, and awarded a sum of Rs.
4,76,432/- alongwith interest @ 9% per annum, from the date of filing the petition, till payment.

3. Parties to the lis, hereinafter, are, referred to, in the same manner, in which, they were referred to,
by the learned Tribunal.

4. Brief facts, leading to filing of the present appeal, before this Court, may be summed up, as under:
Petitioner, Tek Chand has filed the petition under Section 166 of the M.V. Act,
seeking compensation on account of injuries sustained by him in a Motor Vehicle United India Insurance Company vs Tek Chand & Anr on 6 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/118355302/
1 accident, involving vehicle No. HP- 63-0790 (hereinafter referred to as 'the offending vehicle'), owned and driven by respondent No. 1 and insured with respondent No. 2.

According to the pleadings of the petitioner, accident had taken place .
on 31.1.2010 at 9:30 p.m. at Bhangrotu, Tehsil Sadar, District Mandi, H.P., due to rash and negligent driving of respondent No. 1.

4.1 Elaborating his stand, it is the case of the petitioner that he was employed as Conductor/Cleaner with the offending vehicle, owned and driven by respondent No.
1.

On 31.1.2010, when, the offending vehicle was on its way from Bajora to Bhangrotu, then, respondent No. 1 was driving the offending vehicle at a very high speed and when respondent No. 1 was on its way to Bhangrotu, a stray cattle, at once,
came on the road and respondent No. 1, in order to save it, applied the brake, which resulted into skidding of the offending vehicle, which struck with another Truck.
Consequently, the petitioner sustained multiple injuries.
After the accident, he was taken to CHC Ratti, where first aid was given to him.
Thereafter, he was referred to Zonal Hospital, Mandi, where he remained admit w.e.f. 31.1.2010 to 15.3.2010, as indoor patient.
He was operated upon for injuries and plates were inserted in his left leg.
4.2 In addition to this, petitioner has also pleaded .
that due to injuries, sustained by him, he became permanently disabled.

He has spent a sum of Rs.
1,00,000/-, on his treatment.

4.3 It is the further case of the petitioner that he was 42 years of age, at the time of the accident and was employed with respondent No. 1, who used to pay him a sum of Rs. 3500/- per month, as slalary, and a sum of Rs. 100/- per day, as diet money.
5. On the basis of above facts, the petitioner has claimed compensation of Rs. 5,00,000/-, alongwith interest @ 12% per annum, from the date of accident, till realization of the whole amount.
6. When, put to notice, the claim petition was contested by the respondents.
7. Respondent No. 1 has filed reply, in which, he has denied that the accident in question had taken place, due to his rash and negligent driving.
Contents of the claim petition in paras No. 1 to 5 have been admitted.
However, the monthly income of the petitioner has been disputed.
Factum of accident has not been disputed, but, allegations with regard to rash and negligent driving, have been denied, by .

United India Insurance Company vs Tek Chand & Anr on 6 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/118355302/
2 respondent No. 1.
7.1

sentences.text:
Respondent No. 2, Insurance Company has filed its separate reply, by taking preliminary objections that the petition is not maintainable, as according to the investigation conducted by it,
petitioner was driving the alleged vehicle himself, at the time of accident; the petitioner was not having valid and effective driving license and in connivance with the Police, owner of the alleged vehicle has lodged the D.D.R., for the sake of insurance claim; the vehicle in question was being permitted to ply in violation of the terms and conditions of the Insurance Policy.
7.2 Rest of the contents of the claim petition have been denied, for want of knowledge.
Thus, the respondents have prayed for dismissal of the claim petition.

8. From the pleadings of the parties, the learned Tribunal has framed the following issues, vide order dated 17.3.2011:
1.
Whether the petitioner had suffered injuries in a motor vehicle accident bearing registration No. HP 63- 0790 on 31.1.2010, as alleged?
OPP 2.

Whether the respondent no.1 was driving the vehicle .
in a rash and negligent manner which caused the accident, as alleged? OPP.
3.

Whether the petitioner is entitled for the compensation to the extent of Rs 5,00,000/-, if yes,
from whom?
OPP 4.
Whether the petition is not maintainable, as alleged?
OPR 2 5.
Whether the driver was not having any valid driving license?

OPR 2.
6.
Whether the vehicle was being driven in violation of terms and conditions of Insurance Policy and provisions of the M.V.Act, if so its effect?

OPR2.
7. Relief.
9. Thereafter, parties, to the lis, were directed to adduce evidence.
After closure of the evidence and after hearing learned counsel for the parties, the learned Tribunal has allowed the petition, as referred above.

01. Feeling aggrieved from the said award, the Insurance Company, has filed the present appeal,
before this Court, challenging the award passed by the learned Tribunal, mainly on the ground that the learned Tribunal has failed to appreciate the plea set up by the Insurance Company, qua the fact that the offending vehicle was not being driven by the owner of the vehicle, at the relevant time.

11. Elaborating its stand, it has been submitted on .
United India Insurance Company vs Tek Chand & Anr on 6 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/118355302/
3 behalf of the appellant-Insurance Company that the offending vehicle was being driven by the petitioner, who was not having a valid and effective driving license and the DDR was lodged by the owner of the vehicle and the petitioner, in collusion with the Police.
12.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The impugned award has further been assailed on the ground that the learned Tribunal has wrongly held that the Insurance Company could not prove that the offending vehicle was being driven in violation of the terms and conditions of the Insurance Policy.

13. It is the further stand of the appellant- Insurance Company that the learned Tribunal has not considered the fact that claim of the respondent-owner was repudiated by the appellant, vide Ext. RW1/B.
According to the Insurance Company, the petitioner has failed to establish that he has suffered permanent disability, as the disability was with respect to the lower limb only.
14. The amount of the compensation is also stated to be on higher side.

15. On the basis of above facts, Mr. P.S. Chandel, .
learned counsel appearing for the Insurance Company, has prayed that the appeal may kindly be accepted, by setting aside the award, passed by the learned Tribunal.

16. Per contra, Mr. Devender K. Sharma, Advocate appearing for respondent No. 1 and Mr. G.R.
Palsra, Advocate, appearing for respondent No. 2, have supported the impugned award and prayed that the appeal may kindly be dismissed.
17. After framing of the issues, petitioner Tek Chand has examined Dr. Sandeep Vaidya, Orthopedic Surgeon, Zonal Hospital, Mandi.

This witness, being member of the Medical Board, has assessed the disability on the person of the petitioner, on 30.4.20211, and issued the Permanent Disability Certificate with 40% disability, in relation to lower limb.
In addition to this, he has also deposed that the petitioner remained under treatment w.e.f. 31.1.2010 to 15.3.2010.
He has proved the Disability Certificate, Ext. PW1/A.

He has further deposed that the petitioner was again admitted for removing the metal work/plates, on 29.9.2010 and was discharged on .
21.10.2010.
The petitioner was stated to have suffered the fracture of left Tibia, for which, he was operated upon.
17.1 According to this witness, the injuries sustained by the petitioner could be possible in motor vehicle accident.

He has proved the discharge slip, Ext.
PW1/C.
The medical bills pertaining to the petitioner, are Exts. P-1 to P-19.
Lastly, he has deposed that on account of disability, petitioner will face difficulty in working as manual labourer, conductor or driver.

4 17.2.

sentences.text:
In his cross-examination, this witness has deposed that the petitioner was admitted in Zonal Hospital, Mandi, on 31.01.2010, at 11:00 p.m.
18.
Petitioner Tek Chand appeared in the witness box as PW-2 and has filed his affidavit, in evidence, which is based on the pleadings, made in the claim petition.
18.1. In his cross-examination, he has admitted that when, he reached near Bhangrotu, all of a sudden, a stray animal appeared there and in order to save it, the Truck driver has applied the brake.
He was taken to R.H.C. Ratti by the driver of the said truck.
From .
R.H.C. Ratti, he was referred to Zonal Hospital, Mandi.
According to his further deposition, the FIR, regarding the accident in question was lodged, on the next day.
Statement of this witness was recorded by the Police.

18.2 He has further deposed that when, Police came to him, he has disclosed that the accident had not taken place due to his rash and negligent driving, but, the same had taken place, due to the fact that the driver of the truck wanted to save the stray cow.

18.3 Lastly, he has denied the suggestion that since, he was not having the driving license, as such,
respondent No. 1 has been introduced as driver.
19. To rebut this evidence, respondents have examined Nika Ram, working as Assistant with the Insurance Company, as RW-1.
He has proved documents Ext. RW1/A to RW1/F.
The said documents pertain to the investigation report and survey report of the offending vehicle.
19.1. RW-2, Kuldeep Chand Tandon was working with the Insurance Company as Surveyor.

According to him, he has inspected the offending vehicle.
.
According to him, the driver side of the vehicle had suffered more damage.
He has proved photographs Ext. RW1/E and RW1/F.

He has proved the Survey report, Ext. RW1/C.
20.
In cross-examination, even, this witness has admitted that as per his report, Thakur Dass was driver of the offending vehicle.
21. This is the entire evidence led by the parties.

22. The award has been assailed on the ground that the learned Tribunal has not considered the fact that there was collusion between the petitioner and respondent No. 1, and according to the learned counsel, appearing for the Insurance Company, the offending vehicle was being driven by petitioner,
United India Insurance Company vs Tek Chand & Anr on 6 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/118355302/
5 himself.

entities.text: United India Insurance Company vs Tek Chand & Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
23. Insurance Company could not adduce any evidence or produce any document, suggesting the fact that the vehicle was being driven by petitioner himself and not by respondent No. 1.
24.

Further RW-2 himself has admitted that as per the Survey report, Ext. RW1/C, the offending vehicle was being driven by Thakur Dass (respondent No. 1), .
at the relevant time.

Once, the witness of the Insurance Company has himself deposed that the driver of the offending vehicle was respondent No. 1, then, argument of learned counsel for the Insurance Company is liable to be rejected.
Consequently, the same is rejected.

25. The onus is upon the Insurance Company to prove that the offending vehicle was being driven,
in violation of the terms and conditions of the Insurance Policy, but no such evidence has been led by the Insurance-Company, in this regard.
The documents pertaining to offending vehicle have been produced by respondent No. 1.

The evidence of an Assistant, working with the Insurance Company,
who has produced the documents, is too short to hold that the offending vehicle was being driven by petitioner himself, and not by respondent No. 1.
26.
As per document, Ext. PW2/B, respondent No. 1 has got lodged the G.D. entry with Police Station, Balh, District Mandi, mentioning that in the accident, he was neither rash nor negligent.

How it can be expected from a person, who, himself was driving the .
vehicle in a rash and negligent manner, to make a statement, against himself.
27. Petitioner remained admit in hospital, as deposed by PW-1.
The accident in question had taken place on 31.1.2010 and petitioner remained admit w.e.f. 31.1.2010 to 15.3.2010.

He has suffered disability, which, as per the Disability Certificate Ext.
PW1/A is 40%, permanent disability, in relation to lower limb.
The petitioner is proved to be working as Conductor/Cleaner, and according to the deposition of PW-1, he will face difficulty in performing manual labor and working as Conductor.
28. In such situation, the amount of compensation, which has been awarded by the learned Tribunal, does not require any interference.
29. No other point has been urged or argued.

30. With these observations, the present appeal is devoid of merit and the same is dismissed, by upholding the impugned award, dated 2.12.2015, passed by the learned Tribunal in Claim Petition No. 22/2015/2010, titled as, 'Tek Chand versus Thakur Dass & anr.' .
